STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r4.claim: After recalling worldly blessings, the surah tells of Noah's struggle against his people's denial and rebuke and his journey in the ark.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r4.anchor: the sūrah narrates the story of Noah, his struggles with the denial and rebuke of his people, and his journey in the ark (vv. 23–41)

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p544/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p544/r3.speaker: أبو عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p544/r3.claim: Abu Ubayd glosses الغثاء as foam or debris floating on a torrent, something useless.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p544/r3.anchor: الغثاء: الزبد وما ارتفع على السيل ونحو ذلك مما لا ينتفع به قاله أبو عبيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p544/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p544/r4.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p544/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash equates الغثاء and الجفاء: filth and foam carried by a flood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p544/r4.anchor: وقال الأخفش: الغثاء والجفاء واحد، وهو ما احتمله السيل من القذر والزبد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p544/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p544/r5.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p544/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains it as decayed leaves carried by a flood and mixed with its foam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p544/r5.anchor: وقال الزجاج: البالي من ورق الشجر إذا جرى السيل خالط زبده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p544/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p544/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p544/r6.claim: The thāʾ may be geminated or light; its irregular plural is أغثاء, and a line of Imruʾ al-Qays is transmitted with the word in light and doubled forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p544/r6.anchor: وتشدد ثاؤه وتخفف، ويجمع على أغثاء شذوذا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r12.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r12.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the cry was Gabriel's shout that destroyed them; بالحق means their destruction was due because they deserved it, or that God acted justly, and their ruin resembled the flood's decayed black debris.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r12.anchor: قال الزمخشري: صيحة جبريل عليه السلام صاح عليهم فدمرهم بالحق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r13.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the cry was an earthquake.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r14.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r14.claim: Other interpretations identify the cry with the punishment itself, death, or an annihilating punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p562/r14.anchor: وقيل: هي نفس العذاب والموت. وقيل: العذاب المصطلم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r1.claim: The cited poetic line uses صيحة for a cry that makes the people fall on their chins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r1.anchor: صاح الزمان بآل زيد صيحة ... خروا لشنتها على الأذقان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r2.speaker: المفضل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r2.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal explains بالحق as something that cannot be resisted, as in the arrival of death's stupor in truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r2.anchor: وقال المفضل: بالحق بما لا مدفع له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r3.claim: بعدا is an unexpressed verb's verbal noun: they perished; its vocalization varies like the verbal noun of رشد.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r3.anchor: وانتصب بعدا بفعل متروك إظهاره أي بعدوا بعدا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r4.speaker: الحوفي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r4.claim: Al-Ḥawfī attaches للقوم directly to بعدا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats وللقوم الظالمين as an explanatory phrase naming those for whom distance is invoked, rather than as attached to بعدا; Abū Ḥayyān likewise attaches it to an omitted phrase.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p563/r5.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وللقوم الظالمين بيان لمن دعي عليه بالبعد

TABATABAI:23:23-54/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r13.claim: In “the cry seized them in truth,” the preposition bi- may indicate accompaniment or causation; al-ḥaqq may stand for an omitted noun, meaning the true affair or decree.
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r13.anchor: الباء في { بالحق } للمصاحبة وهو متعلق بقوله { فأخذتهم } أي أخذتهم الصيحة أخذا مصاحبا للحق

TABATABAI:23:44-49/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:44-49/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:44-49/r1.claim: Al-ghuthāʾ is debris carried by a flood, such as dried plants, leaves, and worn branches; the word may have a doubled thāʾ.
TABATABAI:23:44-49/r1.anchor: والغثاء بضم الغين وربما شددت الثاء ما يحمله السيل من يابس النبات والورق والعيدان البالية،

TABATABAI:23:44-49/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:44-49/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:44-49/r2.claim: The prayer that the wrongdoers be distanced is a curse, a denunciation, or a supplication against them.
TABATABAI:23:44-49/r2.anchor: وقوله { فبعدا للقوم الظالمين } إبعاد ولعن لهم أو دعاء عليهم.

SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r1.claim: Ghuthāʾ is the second object of jaʿala, which here means to turn them into something.

SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r2.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash glosses ghuthāʾ as jifāʾ, flood-scum or debris; al-Samīn notes the word earlier in al-Raʿd.
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r2.anchor: وقد تقدم في الرعد. قاله الأخفش

SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r3.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines it as decayed leaves that mix with foam when a flood runs.
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج: " هو البالي من ورق الشجر

SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r4.claim: Another gloss is anything useless carried off by a flood or left in a cooking pot; it became proverbial for worthless remains.
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r4.anchor: وقيل: كل ما يلقيه السيل والقدر مما لا ينتفع به

SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r5.claim: In ghuthāʾ the final root radical is wāw, as in ghaṯā al-wādī; the similar nausea verb ghathiyat is from the yāʾ root and is close in sense.
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r5.anchor: ولامه واو لأنه من غثا الوادي يغثو غثوا

SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r6.claim: The word is pronounced with either doubled or light thāʾ; its plural aghthāʾ is irregular, since the expected forms would be aghthiya or ghithyān.
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r6.anchor: وتشدد ثاء " الغثاء " وتخفف وقد جمع على " أغثاء "

SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:41/r7.claim: Al-Samīn cites an Imruʾ al-Qays line using ghuthāʾ alongside flood debris as poetic evidence for the word.

SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r1.claim: Buʿdan is a verbal noun in place of its verb and must be governed by an implicit verb because it expresses a curse or prayer against them.
SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r1.anchor: بعدا: مصدر بدل من اللفظ بفعله

SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r2.claim: The source gives both baʿuda buʿdan and baʿida baʿdan, by analogy with the two forms of rashada rushdan.
SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r2.anchor: والأصل: بعد بعدا وبعدا نحو: رشد رشدا ورشدا

SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the lām as attached to an omitted explanatory phrase, as in suqyā lahu and jadʿan lahu.
SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r3.anchor: كهي في سقيا له وجدعا له. قاله الزمخشري

SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r4.speaker: الحوفي
SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥawfī attaches the lām to buʿdan, but al-Samīn rejects this as unattested.
SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r4.anchor: قاله الحوفي. وهذا مردود؛/ لأنه لا يحفظ حذف هذه اللام

SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r5.claim: In fa-taʿsan lahum, the lām also attaches to an omitted phrase rather than to taʿsan, so it cannot support direct attachment here.
SAMIN-DURR:23:41#2/r5.anchor: ولذلك منعوا الاشتغال في قوله والذين كفروا فتعسا لهم

ZAJJAJ:v4p13/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p13/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p13/r2.claim: Ghuthāʾ is dead, decayed tree foliage seen mixed with foam as a flood flows.
ZAJJAJ:v4p13/r2.anchor: الغثاء الهالك والبالي من ورق الشجر الذي إذا جرى السيل رأيته مخالطا زبده

ASAD-NOTES:23:39/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:39/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:39/r2.claim: A just and unavoidable blast overtakes the evildoers, leaving them like flotsam and scum on a torrent.
ASAD-NOTES:23:39/r2.anchor: And then the blast [of Our punishment) overtook them, justly and unavoidably,[20] and We caused them

ASAD-NOTES:23:39#n20/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:39#n20/r1.speaker: Righib
ASAD-NOTES:23:39#n20/r1.claim: Righib says bi'l-haqq here combines justice, wisdom, reality, inescapability, and suitability to the case, so any translation is approximate.
ASAD-NOTES:23:39#n20/r1.anchor: combines in this instance the concepts of justice, wisdom, reality, inescapability, and consonance with the exigencies of the case under consideration (Righib)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p45#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p45#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p45#4/r1.claim: Qatada glosses the people made into ghuthaʾ as something decayed and worn out.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p45#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فجعلناهم غثاء ﴾ قال الشيء البالي

ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r1.claim: On the view that the people were Thamud, Gabriel's cry destroyed them; if they were ʿAd, this conflicts with reports that a violent wind destroyed them.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r1.anchor: أي صيحة جبريل عليه السلام صاح عليه السلام بهم فدمرهم وهذا على القول بأن القرن قوم صالح

ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r2.claim: To reconcile the ʿAd identification, a report says Gabriel cried out from within the wind; mentioning cry and wind separately suggests either would have sufficed to destroy them.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r2.anchor: وأجاب بأن جبريل عليه السلام صاح بهم من الريح كما روي في بعض الأحاديث

ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r3.claim: Alternatively, الصيحة means a terrible punishment or overwhelming torment, as in the poetic idiom that time cried out against the Barmakids.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r3.anchor: العذاب المصطلم كما في قوله : صاح الزمان بآل برمك صيحة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r4.claim: بالحق attaches to أخذ and means an established, irresistible truth, as in the verse about death's stupor arriving with truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r4.anchor: كما في قوله تعالى : ( وجاءت سكرة الموت بالحق )

ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r5.claim: Other explanations are that the seizure was by God's justice, or fulfilled the messenger's true warning that they would soon regret their actions.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r5.anchor: من قولك : فلان يقضي بالحق إذا كان عادلا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r6.claim: غثاء is flood debris—withered leaves and sticks; أغثاء is an irregular plural, and the ث may be geminated, as in a line by Imruʾ al-Qays about flood debris.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r6.anchor: أي كغثاء السيل وهو ما يحمله من الورق والعيدان البالية ويجمع على أغثاء شذوذا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r7.claim: بعدا can report their distance or function as a curse; distance is opposite nearness, while the second verbal form is used for destruction, and the noun means distance from mercy, good, salvation, or utter ruin.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r7.anchor: يحتمل الإخبار والدعاء والبعد ضد القرب والهلاك وفعلهما ككرم وفرح

ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r8.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r8.claim: In a curse, Sibawayh requires an omitted governor for the verbal noun; the lām identifies those cursed or declared remote and attaches to an omitted expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r8.anchor: ويجب حذف ناصب هذا المصدر عند سيبويه فيما إذا كان دعائيا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r9.claim: The explicit phrase القوم الظالمين replaces a pronoun to signal that their banishment is because of their wrongdoing.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p33#4/r9.anchor: ووضع الظاهر موضع الضمير إيذانا بأن إبعادهم لظلمهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r3.claim: The shout is the cry of punishment.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r4.claim: One explanation takes the shout to mean their destruction.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r5.speaker: جبريل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r5.claim: Another report says Gabriel shouted at them, causing their hearts to split.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: صاح بهم جبريل صيحة فتصدعت قلوبهم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r6.claim: Ghutha means the grasses and tree twigs carried along by a flood.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r6.anchor: {فجعلناهم غثاء} وهو ما يحمله السيل من حشيش وعيدان شجر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r7.claim: God made them dead and dried out like flood-borne vegetation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r7.anchor: معناه: صيرناهم هلكى فيبسوا يبس الغثاء من نبات الأرض،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r8.claim: The verse pronounces ruin and distance from mercy upon the wrongdoing people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417#2/r8.anchor: فبعدا للقوم الظالمين} {ثم أنشأنا من بعدهم قرونا آخرين}

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r1.claim: Gabriel struck them with a terrifying cry that split their hearts and killed them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r1.anchor: جبريل صاح عليهم صيحة هائلة تصدعت منها قلوبهم فماتوا

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r2.claim: This episode identifies the people as Salih's people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r2.anchor: واستدل به على أن القوم قوم صالح

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r3.claim: The cry came inevitably, by God's justice, or according to the true promise.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r3.anchor: بالوجه الثابت الذي لا دافع له

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r4.claim: Their destruction is likened to the debris carried by a flood.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r4.anchor: شبههم في دمارهم بغثاء السيل وهو حميله

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r5.claim: The Arabs say a valley swept someone away to mean that the person perished.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r5.anchor: كقول العرب: سال به الوادي، لمن هلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r6.claim: The phrase may state their doom or pray for it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r6.anchor: يحتمل الإخبار والدعاء، وبعدا مصدر بعد إذا هلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r7.claim: Buʿdan is a verbal noun from baʿuda, governed by an unexpressed verb not ordinarily stated.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r7.anchor: وهو من المصادر التي تنصب بأفعال لا يستعمل إظهارها

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r8.claim: The lām specifies who is prayed against; the explicit description replaces their pronoun to give the reason.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:41/r8.anchor: واللام لبيان من دعي عليه بالبعد، ووضع الظاهر

BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r1.claim: Their destruction follows Noah’s prayer, fulfilling God’s promise to him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r1.anchor: أن تعقب هلاكهم , وعد الله له بذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r2.claim: The cry may be so powerful that it is the only cry of its kind, specifically Gabriel’s cry against Thamud, or it may figuratively mean terrible punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r2.anchor: ويمكن أن تكون على بابها فتكون صيحة جبرئيل عليه الصلاة والسلام ويكون القوم ثمود

BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r3.claim: The punishment was an established, deserved judgment that no one but God could repel, and it was just.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r3.anchor: بالأمر الثابت من العذاب الذي أوجب لهم الذي لا تمكن مدافعته لهم ولا لأحد غير الله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r4.claim: They lay dead like hollow palm trunks and were cast aside like flood debris: vegetation carried by a torrent that blackens, decays, and becomes useless.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r5.claim: God saved their messenger and the believers; the unbelievers perished, while believers prospered and inherited the land.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r5.anchor: ونجينا رسولهم ومن معه من المؤمنين

BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r6.claim: The invocation of distance means destruction and expulsion.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r7.claim: The text states the blameworthy quality instead of a pronoun, making the warning general; these powerful people had no excuse and misused their strength by failing to support the messengers.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p200#2/r7.anchor: أظهر الضمير تعميما وتعليقا للحكم بالوصف تحذيرا لكل من تلبس به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p49#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p49#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p49#2/r1.claim: The stories after Noah show that his people’s fate was part of God’s recurring pattern for those who deny messengers, not a coincidence; the generations are left unnamed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p49#2/r1.anchor: ما أصاب قوم نوح على تكذيبهم له لم يكن صدفة ولكنه سنة الله في المكذبين لرسله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p49#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p49#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p49#2/r2.claim: The unnamed generation is most likely Thamud: the cry fits their destruction by thunderbolt, the prediction of morning regret fits its timing, and their ruins remained at al-Hijr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p49#2/r2.anchor: والأظهر أن المراد به هنا ثمود لأنه الذي يناسبه قوله في آخر القصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r1.claim: The fa suggests that the messenger’s prayer was answered promptly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r1.anchor: تقتضي الفاء تعجيل إجابة دعوة رسولهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r2.claim: Taking them is a metaphor for destroying them.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r3.claim: The cry is the sound of a thunderbolt, which confirms or identifies the destroyed generation as Thamud.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r3.anchor: والصيحة : صوت الصاعقة ، وهذا يرجح أو يعين أن يكون هؤلاء القرن هم ثمود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r4.claim: Attributing destruction to the cry is a rational metaphor: the cry is the cause of destruction or accompanies its cause, the air tearing when the thunderbolt falls.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r4.anchor: وإسناد الأخذ إلى الصيحة مجاز عقلي لأن الصيحة سبب الأخذ أو مقارنة سببه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r5.claim: The bāʾ marks accompaniment: the destruction was just, not an assault, because their wrongdoing made them deserve it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r6.claim: غثاء is what a flood carries, such as dry sticks and leaves.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r6.anchor: والغثاء : ما يحمله السيل من الأعواد اليابسة والورق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r7.claim: This is a concise state simile: like flood debris, they decayed and piled in one place, dying all together.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r7.anchor: والكلام على التشبيه البليغ للهيئة فهو تشبيه حالة بحالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r8.claim: After recounting their denial, the verse curses and demeans them and their likes; it is not a literal prayer, since they have already perished.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r8.anchor: وفرع على حكاية تكذيبهم دعاء عليهم وعلى أمثالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r9.claim: بعدا is an absolute object replacing its verb, like تبا and سحقا, meaning may God send him away and crush him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r9.anchor: وانتصب { بعدا } على المفعولية المطلقة بدلا من فعله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r10.claim: The opposite idiom لا تبعد means ‘do not be lost’; Malik ibn al-Rayb uses it in a verse about his burial.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r10.anchor: وعكس هذا المعنى قول العرب لا تبعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r11.claim: The wrongdoers are the unbelievers: they wronged themselves by associating partners with God and wronged Hud by accusing him of lying about God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r11.anchor: واختير هذا الوصف هنا لأن هؤلاء ظلموا أنفسهم بالإشراك وظلموا هودا لأنه تعمد الكذب على الله إذ قالوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r12.claim: The definite plural is comprehensive, including the people destroyed, and makes the sentence a concluding summary.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r13.claim: The lām clarifies who is meant by the curse; it attaches to an omitted explanatory phrase, making the condemned group explicit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p58/r13.anchor: واللام في { للقوم الظالمين } للتبيين وهي مبينة للمقصود

BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r4.claim: Gabriel's tremendous cry split their hearts and killed them; sayha means a raised voice.
BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r4.anchor: صيحة جبريل صاح عليهم صيحة هائلة تصدعت منها قلوبهم فماتوا

BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r5.claim: Although this suggests Thamud, since Ad were destroyed by a sterile wind, the author reconciles it by suggesting the intensified wind also brought a terrible cry; he cites a report that Shaddad and his family were destroyed by a heavenly cry approaching Iram, or that the cry itself means torment and death.
BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r5.anchor: فإن قلت : هذا يدل على أن المراد بالقرن المذكور في صدر القصة ثمود قوم صالح

BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r6.speaker: الجلالين
BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r6.claim: Al-Jalalayn glosses the cry as the cry of punishment.

BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r7.claim: With truth attaches to the taking and means it occurred by an established, unavoidable decree.
BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r7.anchor: متعلق بالأخذ أي بالوجه الثابت الذي لا دافع له

BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r8.speaker: الجلالين
BURSEVI:v6p59#2/r8.claim: Al-Jalalayn explains the phrase as by God's command.

BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r1.claim: God transformed them into worthless flood debris.
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r1.anchor: أي كغثاء السيل لا ينتفع به وهو ما يحمله

BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r2.claim: Ghuthaʾ is what a flood carries along its surface: foam, leaves, and sticks; the idiom 'the valley swept him away' means that someone perished.
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r2.anchor: وهو ما يحمله السيل على وجهه من الزبد والورق والعيدان

BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r3.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r3.claim: Kashifi glosses the image as destroying and annihilating them, like debris a flood casts aside and leaves black and worn.
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r3.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (غثاء : ون خاشاك آب آورده يعني هلاك كرديم

BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r4.claim: The phrase may report their ruin or curse them.

BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r5.claim: Al-Kashifi glosses it as banishment from God's mercy for the hated oppressors.
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r5.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (س دوري باد ازرحمت خداي مركروه ستمكارانرا)

BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r6.claim: Buʿd means perishing; it is a verbal noun rarely used with an expressed governing verb, and the lām indicates the one addressed by the curse.
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r6.anchor: وبعدا مصدر بعد إذا هلك وهو من المصادر التي لا يكاد يستعمل ناصبها

BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r7.claim: The verse signals the fate of worldly people who rebel against God and transgress against messengers.
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r7.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن أهل الدنيا حين بغوا في الأرض وطغوا على الرسل

BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r8.claim: Though messengers share ordinary people's food and drink, they do not eat with worldly excess: God's people eat without extravagance, unlike disbelievers who consume sevenfold.
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r8.anchor: وقالوا لرسلهم ما قالوا لا يعلمون أن الرسل وأهل الله وإن كانوا يأكلون مما يأكل أهل الدنيا

BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r10.claim: God's people also eat and drink through the mouths of their hearts from divine provision during their nights with their Lord.
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r10.anchor: بل أهل الله يأكلون ويشربون بأفواه القلوب مما يطعمهم ربهم ويسقيهم

BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r11.speaker: أفتاده أفندي
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r11.claim: Aftada says the Prophet stayed with his Lord and received nourishment from varied divine disclosures; outward eating served his weak community, while the stone he strapped on was to keep his subtle spirit in the world for guidance, not because of hunger.
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r11.anchor: قال حضرة الشيخ الشهير بأفتاده أفندي قدس سره : كان عليه السلام يبيت عند ربه

BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r12.claim: The disbelievers had the worst traits: disbelief in the Creator and resurrection, immersion in worldly love, and oppression; their destruction came because of their injustice.
BURSEVI:v6p59#3/r12.anchor: وقد وصف الله الكفار بشر الصفات وهي الكفر بالخالق وبيوم القيامة والانغماس في حب الدنيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#2/r2.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#2/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī identifies the people struck by the cry as Thamūd.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#2/r2.anchor: ومن ذكر الصيحة ذهب الطبري إلى أنهم قوم ثمود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#2/r3.claim: The punishment came justly, because of their deeds and in fulfillment of God's decree concerning their punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#2/r3.anchor: وقوله بالحق معناه بما استحقوا من أفعالهم وبما حق منا في عقوبتهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#2/r4.claim: “Guthāʾ” is the foam and useless debris a flood carries, a comparison for anything lifeless and ruined.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#2/r4.anchor: «الغثاء» ما يحمله السيل من زبده ومعتاده الذي لا ينتفع به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#2/r5.claim: “Buʿdan” is an accusative governed by an omitted verb that is left unspoken.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p144#2/r5.anchor: و «بعدا» منصوب بفعل مضمر متروك إظهاره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#2/r1.claim: The generation after Noah is identified by one view as Ad, who succeeded Noah's people, and by another as Thamud, in light of the cry that seized them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#2/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى أنه أنشأ بعد قوم نوح قرنا آخرين (2) -قيل: المراد بهم عاد، فإنهم كانوا مستخلفين بعدهم. وقيل: المراد بهؤلاء ثمود؛

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#3/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#3/r1.claim: The cry struck them justly because their disbelief and tyranny made them deserve God's punishment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#3/r1.anchor: فأخذتهم الصيحة بالحق} أي: وكانوا يستحقون ذلك من الله لكفرهم وطغيانهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#3/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#3/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir says the apparent account is that the cry struck together with a powerful, cold, violent wind that destroyed everything and left only their homes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#3/r2.anchor: والظاهر أنه اجتمع عليهم صيحة مع الريح الصرصر العاصف القوي الباردة، {تدمر كل شيء بأمر ربها فأصبحوا لا يرى (4) إلا مساكنهم}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#3/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#3/r3.claim: Ghutha means dead bodies cast down like flood debris: worthless, insignificant, ruined things from which nothing can be used.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#3/r3.anchor: وقوله: {فجعلناهم غثاء} أي: صرعى هلكى كغثاء السيل، وهو الشيء الحقير التافه الهالك الذي لا ينتفع بشيء منه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#3/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#3/r4.claim: The evildoers are sent far away for disbelief, defiance, and opposition to their messenger; the audience is warned not to deny its own messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#3/r4.anchor: أي: بكفرهم وعنادهم ومخالفة رسول الله، فليحذر السامعون أن يكذبوا رسولهم.

JISHUMI:v7p5046/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r7.claim: بعدا means may God drive them far away.

JISHUMI:v7p5049/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r10.claim: The cry is explained either as the sound of punishment or as the cry that destroyed Thamūd.
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r10.anchor: قيل: صيحة العذاب، وقيل: هي الصيحة التي أهلكت ثمود

JISHUMI:v7p5049/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r11.claim: One report says an angel cried out, killing them all at once.
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r11.anchor: وقيل: بعث الله ملكا صاح بهم صيحة ماتوا عندها عن آخرهم

JISHUMI:v7p5049/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r12.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r12.claim: Another report identifies Gabriel as the one who cried out at them.
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r12.anchor: عن آخرهم، قيل: صاح بهم جبريل

JISHUMI:v7p5049/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r13.claim: Their punishment was just, a recompense for their disbelief.
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r13.anchor: بالحق أي: على وجه الحق؛ لأنه عاقبهم جزاء على كفرهم

JISHUMI:v7p5049/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r14.claim: غثاء is explained as dead bodies or decayed plant matter carried by a flood; Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and Mujāhid give the latter explanation.
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r14.anchor: (فجعلناهم غثاء) أي: موتى، وقيل: هو المتفتت البالي من الشجر يحتمله السيل

JISHUMI:v7p5049/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r15.claim: One explanation takes their distance as separation from mercy, like a curse; another understands it as a prayer that God drive them away.
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r15.anchor: قيل: بعدا لهم من الرحمة، ونظيره اللعنة التي هي إبعاد من الرحمة

JISHUMI:v7p5049/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r16.claim: The expression is an imprecation, used like سحقا and opposed to لا تبعد; the cited poem uses the latter for the dead.
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r16.anchor: وهذا دعاء، يقال: بعدا لهم وسحقا، ونقيضه: لا تبعد

JISHUMI:v7p5049/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r17.claim: Sending a messenger removes excuses; after disobedience and proof, destruction is deserved. If God created all acts, sending messengers would have no purpose, refuting compulsion about creation, capacity, and will.
JISHUMI:v7p5049/r17.anchor: تدل الآيات على أنه بعث الرسول إزاحة للعنة، فلما خالفوا وجبت عليهم الحجة أهلكوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, and Qatada define ghuthaʾ as decayed vegetation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r4.anchor: أحدها : أنه البالي من الشجر , وهذا قول ابن عباس , ومجاهد , وقتادة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r5.speaker: قطرب
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r5.claim: Qutrub defines ghuthaʾ as leaves that fall into water and then dry.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r5.anchor: والثاني : ورق الشجر إذا وقع في الماء ثم جف , وهذا قول قطرب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r6.speaker: ابن شجرة والأخفش
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r6.claim: Ibn Shajara and al-Akhfash define it as froth and debris carried along by water.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r6.anchor: والثالث : هو ما احتمله الماء من الزبد والقذى , ذكره ابن شجرة وقاله الأخفش .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r7.speaker: ابن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r7.claim: Ibn ʿIsa takes their being distanced as banishment from mercy, like a curse.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r7.anchor: أحدهما : فبعدا لهم من الرحمة كاللعنة , قاله ابن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r8.speaker: أبو بكر النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r8.claim: Abu Bakr al-Naqqash reads it as further distance in punishment and increased ruin.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p53/r8.anchor: الثاني : فبعدا لهم في العذاب زيادة في الهلاك , ذكره أبو بكر النقاش .

MUJAHID:v2p431/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p431/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p431/r1.claim: Ghutha means decayed matter carried along by a flood.
MUJAHID:v2p431/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ فجعلناهم غثاء ﴾ يعني كالرميم الهامد الذي يحمله السيل

MUJAHID:v2p431/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p431/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p431/r2.claim: The people taken by the cry were Thamud.

MUQATIL:23:38-43/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:38-43/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:38-43/r4.claim: The cry was Gabriel's single cry, which killed every one of them.
MUQATIL:23:38-43/r4.anchor: يعنى صيحة جبريل، عليه السلام، فصاح صيحة واحدة فماتوا أجميعن

MUQATIL:23:38-43/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:38-43/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:38-43/r5.claim: Ghuthāʾ is like decayed vegetation carried by a flood; their bodies were likened to that debris.
MUQATIL:23:38-43/r5.anchor: يعنى كالشىء البالي من نبت الأرض يحمله السيل، فشبه أجسادهم بالشىء البالي

MUQATIL:23:38-43/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:38-43/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:38-43/r6.claim: Baʿdan means destruction, and the unjust people here are the polytheists.
MUQATIL:23:38-43/r6.anchor: فبعدا } فى الهلاك { للقوم الظالمين } [آية: 41] يعنى المشركين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r1.claim: Gabriel’s cry struck them and destroyed them.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r1.anchor: أى صيحة جبريل صاح عليهم فدمرهم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r2.claim: “In truth” means justly, as when one says someone judges by the truth, meaning justice.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r2.anchor: بالعدل من الله يقال فلان يقضى بالحق أى بالعدل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r3.claim: Their destruction is likened to flood debris: decayed, blackened leaves and twigs carried by a torrent.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r3.anchor: شبههم فى دمارهم بالغثاء وهو حميل السيل مما بلى واسود من الورق والعيدان

NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r4.claim: Buʿdan means destruction; it is a verbal noun used with an unexpressed verb that is not used explicitly.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r4.anchor: فهلاكا يقال بعد بعدا وأبعد هلك وهو من المصادر المنصوبة بافعال لا يستعمل اظهارها

NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r5.claim: “For the wrongdoing people” identifies those cursed with destruction, like the phrase hīt laka.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#8/r5.anchor: ﴿ للقوم الظالمين ﴾ بيان لمن دعى عليه بالبعد نحو هيت لك

QURTUBI-FULL:23:38-41/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:38-41/r4.speaker: التفاسير
QURTUBI-FULL:23:38-41/r4.claim: Commentaries say Gabriel cried out at them once, together with the wind God used to destroy them, and they all died.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:38-41/r4.anchor: في التفاسير: صاح بهم جبريل عليه السلام صيحة واحدة مع الريح

QURTUBI-FULL:23:38-41/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:38-41/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:38-41/r5.claim: Ghuthāʾ means dead and motionless, like flood debris of rotted and crumbled grasses and reeds.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:38-41/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:38-41/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:38-41/r6.claim: Buʿdan means destruction; another explanation is that they were distanced from God's mercy.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:38-41/r6.anchor: أي هلاكا لهم. وقيل بعدا لهم من رحمة الله

QURTUBI-FULL:23:38-41/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:38-41/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:38-41/r7.claim: Buʿdan is accusative as a verbal noun, like “watering” and “tending.”
QURTUBI-FULL:23:38-41/r7.anchor: وهو منصوب على المصدر. ومثله سقيا له ورعيا

RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r11.claim: Rāzī lists four views of the cry: Gabriel's deadly shout, an earthquake reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, death or punishment according to al-Ḥasan, and overwhelming punishment; he prefers the literal first view.
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r11.anchor: أن جبريل عليه السلام صاح بهم

RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the cry with the earthquake.
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r12.anchor: الصيحة هي الرجفة عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r13.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r13.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the cry is the punishment itself or death, as when one says that a person was called and answered.
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r13.anchor: الصيحة هي نفس العذاب والموت كما يقال فيمن يموت : دعي فأجاب عن الحسن

RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r14.claim: A poetic line about time crying out at the Barmak family illustrates the cry as an overwhelming punishment.

RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r15.claim: Bi-l-ḥaqq means God destroyed them justly, as the phrase judging by truth describes a just judge.

RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r16.speaker: المفضل
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r16.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal says bi-l-ḥaqq means something irresistible, as in the verse about death's stupor arriving with truth.
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r16.anchor: وقال المفضل : بالحق أي بما لا يدفع

RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r1.claim: Ghuthāʾ is the flood-carried debris of decayed, blackened leaves and twigs.

RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r2.claim: The same word describes what God made of the vegetation in another verse.
RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r2.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى : { فجعله غثاء أحوى }

RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r3.claim: The verbal nouns buʿdan, suḥqan, and damran stand in place of verbs and are accusative under verbs whose explicit forms are not used, as Sibawayh explains.
RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r3.anchor: وهي من جملة المصادر التي قال سيبويه

RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r4.claim: Buʿdan means that they perished; the word can be pronounced with either fatḥa or sukūn on the ʿayn, like rushdan.
RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r4.anchor: يقال بعد بعدا وبعدا بفتح العين

RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r5.claim: Buʿdan is like a curse that distances them from goodness; God says it to scorn and humiliate them, and their worldly punishment signals an even greater exclusion from bliss in the Hereafter, warning later generations.
RAZI-FULL:v23p87/r5.anchor: بمنزلة اللعن الذي هو التبعيد من الخير

STUDYQURAN:23:41/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:41/r1.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:23:41/r1.claim: One interpretation identifies the Cry as Gabriel’s literal shout, which causes death itself.
STUDYQURAN:23:41/r1.anchor: literal shout of Gabriel that causes death itself, a great quaking, or the death and punishment themselves (R)

STUDYQURAN:23:41/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:41/r2.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:23:41/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes the Cry to be a great quaking.
STUDYQURAN:23:41/r2.anchor: literal shout of Gabriel that causes death itself, a great quaking, or the death and punishment themselves (R)

STUDYQURAN:23:41/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:41/r3.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:23:41/r3.claim: A further interpretation takes the Cry to mean death and punishment themselves.
STUDYQURAN:23:41/r3.anchor: literal shout of Gabriel that causes death itself, a great quaking, or the death and punishment themselves (R)

STUDYQURAN:23:41/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:41/r4.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:23:41/r4.claim: “Rightly” indicates that the punishment was just.
STUDYQURAN:23:41/r4.anchor: Rightly indicates it was a just punishment (R)

STUDYQURAN:23:41/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:41/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:41/r5.claim: Dross is usually understood as leaves or grass borne on a torrent of water; see 87:5.
STUDYQURAN:23:41/r5.anchor: which is usually understood to mean leaves or grass that are borne on a torrent of water, also see 87:5.

TAB-FULL:v17p46/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r1.claim: God took vengeance by sending the cry, which justly struck them because their disbelief in God and denial of His messenger merited punishment.
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r1.anchor: فانتقمنا منهم، فأرسلنا عليهم الصيحة فأخذتهم بالحق؛

TAB-FULL:v17p46/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r2.claim: Ghuthāʾ is debris floating atop a flood, useless for anything; the verse compares their destruction to something wholly without benefit.
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r2.anchor: وهو ما ارتفع على السيل ونحوه، كما لا ينتفع به في شيء.

TAB-FULL:v17p46/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes them as like dead, decayed tree matter.
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {فجعلناهم غثاء فبعدا للقوم الظالمين} [المؤمنون: 41] يقول: «جعلوا كالشيء الميت البالي

TAB-FULL:v17p46/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r4.claim: Mujāhid likens them to dead, decayed remains carried along by a flood; Ibn Jurayj transmits the same gloss from him.
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r4.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {غثاء} [المؤمنون: 41] «كالرميم الهامد، الذي يحتمل السيل»

TAB-FULL:v17p46/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r5.claim: Qatāda glosses ghuthāʾ as something decayed.
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r5.anchor: عن قتادة: {فجعلناهم غثاء} [المؤمنون: 41] قال: «هو الشيء البالي»

TAB-FULL:v17p46/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says this is a simile God has coined.
TAB-FULL:v17p46/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فجعلناهم غثاء} [المؤمنون: 41] قال: «هذا مثل ضربه الله»

TAB-FULL:v17p47/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p47/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v17p47/r1.claim: The phrase asks that God drive the disbelieving people away through their destruction: they disbelieved in their Lord, disobeyed messengers and wronged themselves.
TAB-FULL:v17p47/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد، قال: " أولئك ثمود، يعني قوله: {فجعلناهم غثاء فبعدا للقوم الظالمين} [المؤمنون: 41] "

TAB-FULL:v17p47/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v17p47/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v17p47/r2.claim: Mujāhid identifies the people in this passage as Thamūd.
TAB-FULL:v17p47/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد، قال: " أولئك ثمود، يعني قوله: {فجعلناهم غثاء فبعدا للقوم الظالمين} [المؤمنون: 41] "

TABRISI:23:41-44/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:41-44/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:41-44/r4.claim: Gabriel’s single cry killed them all.
TABRISI:23:41-44/r4.anchor: صاح بهم جبرائيل صيحة واحدة ماتوا عن آخرهم

TABRISI:23:41-44/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:41-44/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:41-44/r5.claim: The cry was deserved because they disbelieved.

TABRISI:23:41-44/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:41-44/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:41-44/r6.claim: Ghuthaʾ is dried plants and debris carried by floodwater; they were left dead and withered like it.
TABRISI:23:41-44/r6.anchor: وهو ما جاء به السيل من نبات قد يبس وكل ما يحمله السيل على رأس الماء

TABRISI:23:41-44/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:41-44/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:41-44/r7.claim: The curse asks that the unjust polytheists be kept far from mercy.
TABRISI:23:41-44/r7.anchor: أي ألزم الله بعدا من الرحمة { للقوم الظالمين } المشركين

THALABI:v7p46#2/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p46#2/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p46#2/r13.claim: Ghuthā’ is debris carried along by a flood.
THALABI:v7p46#2/r13.anchor: فجعلناهم غثاء وهو ما يحمله السيل

THALABI:v7p46#2/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p46#2/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p46#2/r14.claim: The phrase condemns the unjust people and says they are cast away.
THALABI:v7p46#2/r14.anchor: فبعدا للقوم الظالمين ثم أنشأنا من بعدهم قرونا آخرين

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p297#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p297#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p297#3/r1.claim: Ghuthāʾ means they perished like the foam and debris carried atop a flood, which disperses and goes away.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p297#3/r1.anchor: فجعلناهم غثاء} أي هلكى كالغثاء، وهو ما علا السيل من الزبد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r1.claim: The commentators say Gabriel cried out once, killing them all as their hearts burst.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: صاح بهم جبريل صيحة واحدة ماتوا عن آخرهم بتصدع قلوبهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r2.claim: They deserved the punishment because of their disbelief.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it as the fact that they denied the truth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r3.anchor: وهو معنى قول ابن عباس: يريد حيث كذبوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r4.claim: غثاء is dried vegetation carried by a flood; its regular plurals are أغثية and أغثاء.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r4.anchor: الغثاء: ما جاء به السيل من نبات قد يبس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r5.speaker: امرؤ القيس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r5.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays uses الأغثاء for flood debris as poetic evidence for the word's meaning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r5.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس: من السيل والأغثاء فلكة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r6.speaker: أبو زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r6.claim: Abū Zayd records غثاء الماء and the verb يغثو, describing water laden with dung, leaves, and reeds.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r6.anchor: وقال أبو زيد:] (¬3) غثاء الماء يغثو [وغثاء، إذا كثر فيه البعر والورق والقصب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r7.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r7.claim: The commentators gloss the result as God making them corpses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r7.anchor: قال المفسرون:] (¬5) صيرناهم هلكى (¬6). قال الكلبي:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r8.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r8.claim: Al-Kalbī likens them to dried plant debris that withered.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r8.anchor: قال الكلبي: [يبسوا كما يبس الغثاء من نبت الأرض فهمدوا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r9.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r9.claim: Muqātil says their bodies became like worn-out dry vegetation carried by a flood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p584#2/r9.anchor: وقال] (¬7) مقاتل: جعلناهم كالشيء البالي من نبت (¬8) الأرض يحمل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r1.claim: Their remoteness means distance from mercy, like a curse that removes a person from God's mercy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r1.anchor: أي بعدا لهم من الرحمة، وهي كاللعنة التي هى إبعاد من رحمة الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r2.claim: The sense is that God imposed remoteness upon them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r2.anchor: والمعنى على: ألزمهم الله (¬3) بعدا لهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r3.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r3.claim: Muqātil takes it as remoteness in destruction.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r4.claim: The expression recalls the curse against Midian in Hūd 11:95.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r4.anchor: وذكرنا الكلام في هذا عند قوله: {ألا بعدا لمدين} [هود: 95] الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the wrongdoers as the deniers.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r6.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p586/r6.claim: Muqātil identifies the wrongdoers as polytheists.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:39-41/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:39-41/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:39-41/r3.claim: God's commanded cry of punishment killed them, leaving them still like flood-borne debris, including decayed tree matter.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:39-41/r3.anchor: صيحة العذاب { بالحق } بالأمر من الله تعالى { فجعلناهم غثاء } هلكى هامدين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:39-41/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:39-41/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:39-41/r4.claim: “Perdition” means destruction, and the wrongdoers here are the polytheists.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401/r3.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401/r3.claim: Hasan explains the blast as punishment.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401/r4.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401/r4.claim: Mujahid, through al-Mu'alla and Abu Yahya, compares the people made into debris to something decayed.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401/r4.anchor: في تفسير المعلى عن أبي يحيى عن مجاهد

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401/r5.speaker: بعضهم
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401/r5.claim: Some compare them to vegetation that is crushed after it was green.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم: مثل النبات إذا صار غثاء، فتهشم بعد إذ كان أخضر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p401/r6.claim: The wrongdoers driven away are the polytheists.

ELMALILI:23:31-41/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:31-41/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:31-41/r12.claim: A cry seizes the people justly; God sweeps them away like flood scum and declares the wicked far removed.
ELMALILI:23:31-41/r12.anchor: Biz onları bir gusâ hâline getiriverdik yani bir sel köpüğü gibi savuruverdik {فَبُعْدًۭا لِّلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ} artık defolsun öyle zâlimler.

MAJAZ:v2p59/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p59/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p59/r1.claim: Guthāʾ is foam-like material floating on a flood, useless for anything.
MAJAZ:v2p59/r1.anchor: فجعلناهم غثاء » (41) وهو ما أشبه الزبد وما ارتفع على السيل وما أشبه ذلك مما لا ينتفع به فى شىء.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r1.speaker: Eski müfessirlerin bir kısmı
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r1.claim: Some early commentators identify the unnamed generation as Thamūd and its prophet as Ṣāliḥ.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r1.anchor: Eski müfessirlerin bir kısmı, bu âyetlerde ismi verilmeden kendisinden söz edilen neslin Semûd kavmi ve onlara gönderilen peygamberin Sâlih aleyhisselâm olduğu kanaatindedirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r2.speaker: çoğunluk
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r2.claim: Most commentators identify the unnamed generation as ʿĀd and its prophet as Hūd.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r2.anchor: çoğunluk tarafından ise bu neslin Âd kavmi, peygamberin de Hûd aleyhisselâm olduğu söylenmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r3.speaker: Muhammed Esed
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r3.claim: Esed reads the passage as a general reference to recurring patterns in the lives and experiences of all God’s prophets, without naming a particular prophet or people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r3.anchor: bu âyetlerde belli bir peygamber ve kavimden söz edilmediği

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r4.claim: The author agrees with Esed that the passage describes a common prophetic experience rather than one specific prophet and people.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r7.claim: Since the Qur’an answers these denials of the prophet’s person and of the afterlife elsewhere, this passage only warns of the rejecters’ painful fate.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r7.anchor: burada bir defa daha tekrarlanmasına gerek görülmemiş, sadece uğrayacakları acı âkıbete dikkat çekilmekle yetinilmiştir

ITQAN:v4p378/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p378/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p378/r7.claim: Ghayy, Atham, Mwbq, Saʿir, Wayl, Saʾil, and Suhaq are valleys in Hell.
ITQAN:v4p378/r7.anchor: وغي وأثام وموبق والسعير وويل وسائل وسحق أودية في جهنم

ITQAN:v4p378/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p378/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ITQAN:v4p378/r13.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr calls Saʿir a valley of pus in Hell and Suhaq a valley in Hell.
ITQAN:v4p378/r13.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال السعير واد من قيح في جهنم وسحق واد في جهنم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#4/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#4/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#4/r8.claim: The definite “the people” in 23:41 identifies a particular people, Ṣāliḥ’s nation, confirmed by their destruction; the indefinite “a people” in 23:44 is general, since successive generations and messengers are described.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#4/r8.anchor: الأولى في قوم معينين وهم قوم صالح
